title: This song of mine is a flowing fountain of light
lead: The second song of the cycle is dedicated to unbending determination. It is important for the student to pay attention to compound verbs of motion ("bahe jai", "bhenge jai") signifying continuous ongoing action, and the imagery of a mountain stream sweeping away all obstacles.

words.note: Points to the song of the singer

lines.structure: "E gan amar" (subject with modifiers) + "alor jharnadhara" (nominal part of predicate with copula [is])
lines.literal: This song of mine light's fountain stream.
lines.natural: This song of mine is a flowing fountain of light.

words.meaning_here: along the way, on the trail

lines.structure: "Upala pathe" (adverbial of place) + "dine rate" (paired adverbial of time: day and night)
lines.literal: Along rocky path by day [and] by night,
lines.natural: Along the rocky path, both day and night,

words.form: pres. tense, 1st person (-i), auxiliary verb of continuous action
words.meaning_here: I go, I keep on moving

lines.structure: Compound verbal predicate "bahe jai" (I keep flowing), subject "I" implied by 1st-person form
Predicate "bahe jai" + predicative modifier "bandhana hara" to 1st person pronoun
lines.literal: I flow unrestrained, having lost all bonds,
lines.natural: I keep on flowing forward, free from all bonds,

lines.structure: Nominative phrase-refrain repeating key image of first line

words.role: first part of compound nominal predicate
words.note: Sanskrit bandhura (uneven, hilly). Not to be confused with "bandhu" (friend)

lines.structure: "E path amar" (subject with modifiers) + "bandhura kantakabhara" (homogeneous nominal predicates with copula [is])
lines.literal: This path of mine rugged, with thorns full.
lines.natural: This path of mine is rugged and full of thorns.

words.form: postposition of ablative case (hote / poetic h'te)

words.meaning_here: of vital force, of breath of life
in stream, by force of stream

lines.structure: "Utsa hate" (adverbial of source) + "pranera srote" (adverbial of instrument/manner, relates to predicate "bhenge jai")
lines.literal: From source by stream of life
lines.natural: From the very source, in a surging stream of life,

lines.structure: Compound verbal predicate of intensive/continuous action with implied subject "I"
lines.natural: I keep shattering on my way,

words.meaning_here: I go, I keep on shattering

lines.structure: Predicate "bhenge jai" + direct object "pashan kara" (stone prison)
lines.natural: I keep shattering the granite prison walls,

lines.structure: Nominative refrain closing stanza and connecting it to original source

heard: In subtitles and singing, forms bahe ja'i and bheunge ja'i are repeated twice, as marked in the musical score
In the first line of the second part, the subtitles omit the line "E path a'ma'r bandhura kant'akabhara'", but in the audio recording the singer sings it exactly according to text
interpretation: The image of a spring stream of light embodies the individual soul and its unyielding spiritual determination (sádhaná). The spiritual seeker's path is never smooth: it is strewn with stones of hardships and thorns of doubts ("upala pathe", "kantakabhara"). Yet the spiritual stream originates in the supreme Boundless ("Utsa hate") and is therefore endowed with irresistible force ("pranera srote"). The stone prison ("pashan kara") represents the shackles of ignorance, dogma, ego, and narrow-mindedness, which this divine stream relentlessly smashes to pieces on its way to the ocean of Supreme Consciousness.
